p: The ad begins with a hook asking who reviews agent-written specs, then demonstrates inline commenting on a rendered decision doc. It switches to a terminal running a Claude command to apply the review comments, shows the updated doc with shortened timelines at the same URL, and confirms the comment thread is marked resolved.
Teams can review and comment directly on AI-generated documentation, allowing the AI agent to update the spec at the same URL.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Hook displays over an out-of-focus document preview."},{"timestamp":"00:06","observation":"Zoomed view shows text highlighting and a comment being submitted."},{"timestamp":"00:11","observation":"Terminal sequence demonstrates the AI CLI applying comments to modify the spec."},{"timestamp":"00:17","observation":"Updated artifact renders with modified scope under the same URL."},{"timestamp":"00:23","observation":"End screen displays core value proposition and website URL."}]

The demonstration delivers a clear, focused narrative aligned with developer workflows. Text legibility is maintained throughout despite the compact mobile viewport. Motion and UI transitions are stable, though the pacing in the terminal sequence is slightly subdued.

p: ["hook is a decision-doc screenshot, not a strong scroll-stopper","brand/product identity (artifactshare.com) only appears in final frame, low salience throughout","no explicit CTA action shown (no 'try it' button or click prompt)","narrative relies on reading small on-screen text, slower to parse in-feed"]

Clean, coherent screen-recording style with no rendering defects and a legible narrative arc (comment -> agent edit -> republish -> decision made), which supports message_clarity well. But the hook frame is a dense document screenshot with a caption line, not visually arresting, so it risks scroll-past before the payoff registers. Product identity (artifactshare.com, the actual product chrome) is mostly implicit until the last card, weakening product_salience and cta_intent versus a design that keeps the URL/brand visible throughout. Good for a considered, caption-reading developer audience but not optimized for thumb-stopping in a fast feed.
